SMTO-AUT-0033 — SMTO couldn't confirm which Google account signed in

GUID: 73e32bd1-887d-5d3a-b5ce-bb3e92e197c1
Slug: google-identity-mismatch
Domain: AUT · Subsystem: google-workspace

What happened

  • After you signed in, SMTO couldn't verify Google's proof of which account it was, so it didn't save the connection. Your existing connections weren't changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO for a new Google sign-in link, open it right away, and finish signing in without reusing any older link. Google's proof is tied to that one sign-in request, so an old or mixed-up link can't be verified.
  2. Make sure the computer running SMTO shows the correct date and time and can reach Google. SMTO checks the time stamps in Google's proof and downloads Google's signing keys, so a wrong clock or blocked connection makes the check fail.
  3. If it still fails, ask the person who manages SMTO to check that the client ID in the Google Workspace OAuth App entry matches the app in Google Cloud. Google's proof names the app it was issued for, and SMTO rejects it if that doesn't match the saved client ID.

What success looks like

  • The Google sign-in tab says your email is connected and you can close the window.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Don't edit a Google account entry by hand to add the email or identity; SMTO only trusts details verified by Google.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Google ID token verification failed (signature, issuer, audience or authorized party, expiry, nonce, or verified-email claim), so the signed-in identity was not saved.

What this means

  • Google identity verification failed the signed-claim, audience, issuer, nonce, expiry or verified-email requirements. Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.

Why this can happen

  • Google identity verification failed the signed-claim, audience, issuer, nonce, expiry or verified-email requirements.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the validation stage and registered application identity; keep the signed token private and restart with matching consent state.

How to fix it

  • Restart consent with auth.google_connect for the intended identity. If it repeats, check the Server clock (30-second leeway on exp and iat), that the Server can fetch https://www.googleapis.com/oauth2/v3/certs, and that the google_oauth_app client_id matches the ID token audience; the account's email must be verified by Google.
  • Restart consent for the intended Google identity. Signature, audience, issuer, nonce and verified email must match the application.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm account identity and required features before retrying.

How to verify the fix

  • Signature and required claims verify for the intended client and the email is provider-verified.

What not to do

  • Do not expose client secrets, tokens, codes or PKCE verifiers.
  • Do not switch accounts or repeat uncertain mutations automatically.

Technical notes

  • Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
